search_log: Searched “State of Terror Hillary Rodham Clinton Louise Penny excerpt publisher” and opening/first-chapter variants; the Simon & Schuster page supplied catalog material but no prose excerpt, while Everand exposed a sustained English preview.
Searched the title with “point of view,” “third person,” “narrator,” and “multiple narrators”; opened BookRags' explicit POV description and SuperSummary's chapter-level structural analysis.

Searched exact opening and interior phrases plus Google Books, Macmillan, People, Penguin, and translated-edition leads; Google Books mainly exposed catalog text, the People excerpt was not discoverable directly, and the Penguin Spanish page timed out.

Opened additional German translated preview material and Google Books bibliographic pages as corroborating/discovery material, but omitted them from usable evidence because the English licensed preview and explicit structural sources were stronger.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, with shifting focalization among Ellen Adams and other characters. The licensed opening preview sustains this structure across several scenes and character viewpoints, and the explicit web descriptions corroborate it. Goodreads event passages q06142, q06146, and q06159 independently expose compatible third-person narration, including access to characters' knowledge or unspoken impulses. First-person forms in the quote set occur in dialogue or unresolved clipped material, not in a sustained narratorial strand. The main limitation is that the Tier A preview covers only the opening chapters, but the interior Goodreads passages and whole-book POV description provide consistent corroboration with no credible contrary evidence.
